Alkanes are nearly non-polar because their bonding electrons are shared almost equally. They therefore lack charged or reactive sites for many reagents to attack.
When ignited, natural gas mixed with air burns rapidly and releases a large amount of heat, which can cause an explosion.
Sunlight, particularly its UV radiation, supplies energy to initiate the photochemical substitution reaction.
Combustion releases a large amount of heat, making alkanes useful as fuels for cooking, heating and other energy needs.
Leaked natural gas mixes with air and can explode if ignited. Close the gas valve, avoid flames and sparks, and ventilate the area safely.
